newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli, Jordanian firms talk on $60 mln venture.
newsitem.headline: Israeli, Jordanian firms talk on $60 mln venture.

text.p: Haifa Chemicals is negotiating with Jordan's Arab Potash Co to set up a $60 million joint venture in Jordan, a spokesman for the Israeli company said on Thursday.
"The joint venture would be for the setting up of a plant to produce raw materials for our Israeli plants," the spokesman said, adding that negotiations were in their initial stages.
Haifa Chemicals is the world's leading producer of the fertiliser potassium nitrate.
Haifa Chemicals has two plants in Israel -- one in Haifa and the other at Mishor Rotem, in the Negev desert. The Haifa plant is currently shut down because of a dispute over a wage agreement.

The company spokesman said despite the shutdown, Haifa Chemicals would continue to supply customers from its Mishor Rotem plant as well as from a plant in Vicksburg, Mississippi, owned by Trans Resources Inc, parent company of Haifa Chemicals.
